name: P4 — Direction-specific rubric
description: P4: completeness and scientific quality under the accompanying task specification. Integrity is evaluated in the separate integrity rubric.

deliverables.title: Deliverable presence (Tier 1 gates)
deliverables.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does proposal/report.pdf exist in the workspace and contain readable content (not zero bytes, not a placeholder)?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check: stat proposal/report.pdf. If present, open it to verify it's a non-trivial PDF (> 4 pages or > 1000 words of content).

yes.description: report.pdf exists and contains substantive content.
yes.criteria: File exists at proposal/report.pdf, is a valid PDF, and contains a meaningful paper (introduction, methodology, results, etc.). Not a placeholder or stub.

no.criteria: Either the file does not exist, is malformed, or contains essentially no substantive content (placeholder, blank, single sentence).

leaves.question: Does proposal/logs/ exist and contain non-empty log files?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check: ls proposal/logs/. Inspect a few of the files for actual run output (timestamps, metrics, configuration records).

yes.description: logs directory exists with run records.
yes.criteria: proposal/logs/ exists and contains files documenting the actual execution of the experiments — at minimum, baseline_verification and proposed_method runs.

no.criteria: Directory absent, empty, or contains only placeholder/empty files.

leaves.question: Do logs exist for the SMART and gSMART baseline runs?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/: look for baseline_verification/, smart/, gsmart/, or similarly named subdirectories with run output.

yes.description: SMART and gSMART runs are logged.
yes.criteria: Log files exist for runs of both SMART and gSMART acquisition strategies on the test functions.

no.description: Baseline runs are absent from logs.
no.criteria: No log entries for SMART runs, or no log entries for gSMART runs.

leaves.question: Do logs exist for the proposed acquisition method runs?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/: look for proposed-method/, or a subdirectory named after the agent's method.

yes.criteria: Log files exist documenting at least one run of the proposed acquisition method on the test functions.

no.criteria: No logged runs of any new acquisition strategy distinct from random/grid/SMART/gSMART.

leaves.question: Does the paper contain a Methodology (or equivalently named) section that describes the proposed acquisition criterion?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex or report.pdf: section structure.

yes.criteria: The paper has a section explicitly describing the proposed method (titled Methodology, Methods, Approach, or similar) with substantive content.

no.criteria: No section dedicated to describing the proposed method, or such a section exists but is empty/placeholder.

leaves.question: Does the paper contain an Analysis (or equivalently named) section that discusses mechanism, failure, or compute aspects beyond the bare results?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex or report.pdf: section structure.

yes.criteria: The paper has a dedicated section (Analysis, Discussion, or similar) that goes beyond reporting numbers to discuss why the method works, where it fails, or its compute cost.

no.criteria: No section beyond Experimental Results that interprets or analyzes the results.

leaves.question: Is a main results table present in the paper, labeled tab:main_results, comparing the proposed method to baselines across (function, budget) configurations?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex: search for \label{tab:main_results} or equivalent.

yes.description: Main results table is present and labeled tab:main_results.
yes.criteria: A table exists with label tab:main_results (or a clearly equivalent label that the prose references as the main results table) and reports proposed method vs baselines per configuration.

no.criteria: No table comparing proposed method to baselines, or no table labeled tab:main_results.

leaves.question: Are convergence curves (reconstruction error vs number of measurements) present in the paper?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex figures and proposal/code/ figure-generation scripts.

yes.criteria: At least one figure in the paper plots reconstruction error against measurement budget for at least the proposed method and the SMART/gSMART baselines.

no.criteria: No figure plots error vs budget for the proposed method and baselines.

leaves.question: Does proposal/codebase_notes.md exist with substantive content (not empty, not placeholder)?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem: cat proposal/codebase_notes.md.

yes.criteria: File exists and contains an inspection record of gpCAM, Bluesky, and SciAnalysis: what was found in each, what was reused, what was bypassed and why.

no.criteria: File absent, empty, or contains placeholder/single-line content with no inspection record.

leaves.question: Does proposal/attempts_log.md exist when the paper describes partial work, failed experiments, or unresolved items?
leaves.evidence: proposal/attempts_log.md plus proposal/report.tex to determine whether any contract item is described as partial/failed/unresolved.

tiers.name: not_required_no_partial_work
tiers.description: Paper claims complete work; attempts_log not required.
tiers.criteria: Paper describes no contract item as partial, failed, or unresolved, and reports outperformance on all configurations.

tiers.name: required_and_present_substantive
tiers.description: Paper describes partial work; attempts_log is present and substantive.
tiers.criteria: At least one configuration shows a non-win, OR the paper describes any work as partial/abandoned/attempted-but-failed. proposal/attempts_log.md exists and documents distinct approaches tried with reasoning.

tiers.name: required_and_present_thin
tiers.description: attempts_log present but content is thin.
tiers.criteria: Partial work claimed; attempts_log exists but documents fewer than 2 distinct approaches or lacks reasoning.

tiers.name: required_and_missing
tiers.description: attempts_log required but absent or empty.
tiers.criteria: Paper describes partial/failed work or has losses, but attempts_log.md is missing or empty.

method_specification.title: Proposed method specification
method_specification.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is the proposed acquisition criterion stated in the Methodology section before any empirical results are described?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex section ordering.

yes.criteria: The Methodology section names the method, gives its mathematical/algorithmic form, and motivates it. This appears before any results tables, figures, or numerical claims.

no.criteria: Method is revealed only via results, or Methodology section is absent/empty, or method specification appears after results.

leaves.question: Is the mathematical form of the acquisition function given explicitly (formula, not just verbal description) and sufficient for a domain expert to reimplement?
leaves.evidence: Methodology section equations and prose.

yes.criteria: The paper provides a complete formula or precise algorithmic description that an expert in active learning could reimplement without consulting the code.

no.description: Mathematical form is missing or incomplete.
no.criteria: Only verbal description; key terms undefined; critical quantities left ambiguous; or formula present but missing critical components.

leaves.question: Are the proposed method's required hyperparameters listed with concrete values sufficiently completely to reproduce the scientific protocol? Whether quoted values contradict executed values is assessed only in integrity.
leaves.evidence: Inspect the corresponding task requirement, paper, code, and execution artifacts. Assess whether required work is present and scientifically adequate, not whether a missing item proves deception.

satisfied.description: The applicable scientific/documentation requirement is satisfied.
satisfied.criteria: Affirmatively establish every applicable component of the question from the submitted evidence and the task. Use the task's actual numerical thresholds and allowed alternatives; absence of a demonstrated problem is not sufficient.

not_satisfied.description: Required work is missing, incomplete, or scientifically noncompliant; describe the specific shortfall.

insufficient_evidence.description: The submitted evidence cannot establish whether the applicable scientific requirement is satisfied. This is not a pass and is not an integrity finding.

not_applicable.description: The task makes this conditional/optional and its antecedent is absent; explain the task-supported reason. An unconditional requirement cannot be waived this way.

leaves.question: Does the motivation for the method connect to active-learning, Bayesian-experimental-design, or surrogate-modeling literature, beyond intuitive justification?
leaves.evidence: Methodology section prose and citations.

yes.description: Motivation cites and engages with relevant literature.
yes.criteria: The paper grounds the method in established concepts (information gain, expected improvement, IMSE, query-by-committee, etc.) with specific citations and substantive engagement.

no.criteria: Motivation reads as 'this seemed like a good idea' without citing or building on prior work.

leaves.question: Is the proposed acquisition implemented as a gpCAM-compatible component (custom acquisition plugged into gpCAM's pipeline), or if not, does the paper justify the alternative implementation?
leaves.evidence: proposal/code/: inspect how the method is implemented relative to gpCAM. proposal/codebase_notes.md may explain the decision.

tiers.name: gpcam_integrated
tiers.description: Proposed method runs through gpCAM as a custom acquisition function.
tiers.criteria: The proposed acquisition is plugged into gpCAM's existing pipeline, sharing surrogate/optimizer code with the SMART/gSMART baselines so the only difference is the acquisition criterion.

tiers.name: non_gpcam_with_justification
tiers.description: Implementation is outside gpCAM but the paper or codebase_notes explains why.
tiers.criteria: Implementation does not use gpCAM, but the rationale is stated explicitly.

tiers.name: non_gpcam_no_justification
tiers.description: Implementation is outside gpCAM with no stated rationale.
tiers.criteria: The method is implemented from scratch or via an unrelated framework, and neither the paper nor codebase_notes addresses why gpCAM wasn't used.

baseline_verification.title: Baseline verification
baseline_verification.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is SMART run via gpCAM (not reimplemented from scratch) on all five test functions at all measurement budgets with 10 seeds each?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/baseline_verification/ or equivalent; proposal/code/ to verify gpCAM is the underlying engine.

yes.description: SMART runs are complete across functions/budgets/seeds via gpCAM.
yes.criteria: Logs document gpCAM-based SMART runs covering Piecewise I/II, Smooth Oscillatory, Non-differentiable, 3D Diffusion at every budget the contract specifies, with 10 seeds each.

no.description: SMART runs incomplete or not via gpCAM.
no.criteria: Some functions/budgets/seeds missing, OR SMART was reimplemented outside gpCAM, OR coverage gaps.

leaves.question: Is gSMART run via gpCAM on all five test functions at all measurement budgets with 10 seeds each, using a single fixed weight value across functions?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/ for gSMART runs; check that the weight parameter (paper uses c=20 in equation 10) is identical across function runs.

yes.description: gSMART runs complete with single fixed weight.
yes.criteria: Logs document gpCAM-based gSMART runs across all functions/budgets/seeds, with the same numerical weight value used in every function's runs.

no.description: gSMART runs incomplete or use varying weights.
no.criteria: Coverage gaps, OR per-function weight tuning, OR gSMART reimplemented outside gpCAM.

leaves.question: Are random sampling and uniform grid baselines run on all five test functions at all measurement budgets with 10 seeds each?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/ for random and grid baseline runs.

yes.description: Random and grid baselines run completely.
yes.criteria: Both random and grid baselines logged for all functions/budgets/seeds.

no.criteria: Either baseline missing entirely, or coverage gaps for some functions/budgets/seeds.

leaves.question: Do the reproduced SMART/gSMART baselines show qualitative behavior consistent with the original paper (clearly outperforming random/grid at matched budgets, monotonic improvement vs budget)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex baseline-verification figures; cross-check with paper.md Figures 3–7 in the original.

yes.description: Baselines qualitatively match the original paper.
yes.criteria: SMART and gSMART achieve lower error than random and grid at matched budgets, and error decreases monotonically (or near-monotonically) with budget. Exact numerical match not required.

no.criteria: SMART/gSMART do not beat random/grid, or error does not decrease with budget, indicating either a misimplementation or test-function mismatch.

experimental_completeness.title: Experimental sweep completeness
experimental_completeness.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is the proposed method run on all 21 (function, budget) configurations?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/proposed_method/; cross-check against the main results table.

yes.criteria: Logs document proposed-method runs for: 4 budgets × 4 2D functions (Piecewise I/II, Smooth Osc., Non-diff.) + 5 budgets × 1 3D function (Diffusion) = 21 configurations.

no.criteria: Logs cover fewer than 21 distinct (function, budget) configurations for the proposed method.

leaves.question: Is each configuration run with 10 independent random seeds, with mean and std reported in the paper?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/ for seed enumeration; results table cells for mean ± std reporting.

yes.description: 10 seeds per configuration, mean ± std reported.
yes.criteria: Every (function, budget) configuration has 10 distinct logged seed runs, and the paper reports mean and standard deviation across them.

no.description: Fewer seeds, or no uncertainty reported.
no.criteria: Some configurations have fewer than 10 seeds, or results are point estimates without uncertainty.

leaves.question: Within each seed run, do all methods (random, grid, SMART, gSMART, proposed) start from the same initial 10 random points?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/ for initial-design records; proposal/code/ for initial-point sampling logic.

yes.description: Initial designs are paired across methods.
yes.criteria: Within a single seed, all five methods receive the identical initial 10 random points before each method starts its adaptive acquisitions.

no.description: Each method samples its own initial design.
no.criteria: Methods receive independent initial points within a seed (uncontrolled variance), or the initial-design pairing is not implemented.

leaves.question: Does the headline comparison fit the proposed method's hyperparameters with one principled selection procedure applied identically across all five test functions (fitted values may differ per function; a hand-tuned per-function variant only in clearly-labeled additional rows)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/proposed_method/ for the hyperparameter-fitting records across function runs; proposal/report.tex for any hand-tuned per-function rows.

yes.description: One principled selection procedure applied across functions; hand-tuned variants labeled.
yes.criteria: All headline (function, budget) runs of the proposed method fit hyperparameters with the same principled selection procedure (e.g., marginal likelihood or least squares, as the variogram parameter is fit); the fitted values may differ per function. If a hand-tuned per-function variant is also reported, it appears as a separately-labeled row, not as the headline.

no.criteria: The headline hyperparameters are hand-tuned per function, or the selection procedure is switched between functions, rather than one principled rule applied identically to produce every function's fitted values.

metric_reporting.title: Modern predictive-quality metric reporting
metric_reporting.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Are RMSE, CRPS, and a probability-coverage (calibration) curve reported for the proposed method and the SMART/gSMART/random/grid baselines, computed from the surrogate posterior on the dense held-out grid?
leaves.evidence: Supplementary metrics table and calibration figure in the report; metric values in proposal/logs/.

yes.description: All three modern metrics reported for all methods.
yes.criteria: RMSE, CRPS, and a coverage curve appear for the proposed method and the baselines.

no.criteria: One or more of RMSE/CRPS/coverage is absent, or reported only for a subset of methods.

leaves.question: Were the modern metrics recomputed for the paper's own methodology (SMART and gSMART) and compared head-to-head against the proposed method, rather than reported only for the proposed method?
leaves.evidence: Supplementary metrics table comparing methods; proposal/logs/ baseline metric computations.

yes.description: Baselines scored on the modern metrics too.
yes.criteria: RMSE/CRPS/coverage are computed for SMART/gSMART and compared against the proposed method.

no.criteria: Modern metrics are reported only for the proposed method, with no recomputed baseline comparison.

outperformance.title: Faster convergence per test function
outperformance.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: On the piecewise_I test function, classify the convergence speedup of the proposed method against BOTH SMART and gSMART, based on per-budget mean ± std reconstruction error.
leaves.evidence: From proposal/report.tex main results table and proposal/logs/, extract the per-budget (mean, std) for SMART, gSMART, and proposed on this function. Compute: (a) the smallest tested budget B* at which proposed_mean[B*] ≤ min(SMART_mean[B_max], gSMART_mean[B_max]), where B_max is the largest tested budget for this function (500 for 2D, 1000 for 3D); (b) for each tested budget B, whether proposed_mean[B] < min(SMART_mean[B], gSMART_mean[B]) and whether the gap exceeds 1 std (per-method std, conservative test); (c) whether any budget shows proposed_mean[B] > min(SMART_mean[B], gSMART_mean[B]) by >1 std.

tiers.name: substantial_speedup
tiers.description: ≥2× sample efficiency: proposed reaches baselines' max-budget error at ≤50% of the max budget, with ≥1 std dominance at the majority of budgets.
tiers.criteria: BOTH of the following hold: (1) B*/B_max ≤ 0.5 (proposed reaches baselines' max-budget error using at most half the budget; interpolate linearly between tested budgets if needed); (2) at the majority of tested budgets, proposed_mean + proposed_std ≤ min(SMART_mean, gSMART_mean).

tiers.name: modest_speedup
tiers.description: Consistent dominance with 20–50% budget savings: proposed_mean ≤ both baselines at every budget, and reaches max-budget baseline error at 50–80% of max budget.
tiers.criteria: BOTH of the following hold: (1) B*/B_max ∈ (0.5, 0.8] (proposed reaches baselines' max-budget error using 50–80% of the budget); (2) proposed_mean ≤ min(SMART_mean, gSMART_mean) at every tested budget (consistent dominance, gap may be within noise). Substantial speedup criteria are NOT met.

tiers.name: matches
tiers.description: Curves overlap within noise — no clear advantage either direction.
tiers.criteria: Neither substantial nor modest speedup criteria are met, AND no budget shows proposed_mean exceeding at least one baseline by >1 std. Curves are essentially indistinguishable within noise.

tiers.name: slight_regression
tiers.description: Proposed is worse than at least one baseline at some budgets but within 1 std (noise-level slowdown).
tiers.criteria: Proposed_mean > min(SMART_mean, gSMART_mean) at some tested budgets, but the gap is within 1 std at every such budget. Speedup criteria are not met. The slowdown is real but small.

tiers.name: clear_regression
tiers.description: Proposed is meaningfully worse than at least one baseline by >1 std at multiple budgets.
tiers.criteria: Proposed_mean exceeds min(SMART_mean, gSMART_mean) by more than 1 std at two or more tested budgets. This is a real slowdown that contradicts the method's value proposition for this function.

mechanism_analysis.title: Mechanism analysis
mechanism_analysis.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the Analysis section contain an explicit subsection on mechanism (why the method achieves lower error)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex Analysis section structure.

yes.criteria: A subsection of Analysis is dedicated to explaining the mechanism behind the proposed method's advantage. The subsection title need not be literally 'Mechanism' but must be clearly mechanism-focused.

no.criteria: Analysis section has no dedicated mechanism subsection (mechanism discussion may exist in prose but isn't structurally separated).

leaves.question: Is the mechanism supported by either an ablation, a sensitivity analysis, or theoretical reasoning grounded in the active-learning literature?
leaves.evidence: Methodology and Analysis sections; supporting figures/tables.

yes.criteria: The mechanism claim is backed by at least one of: (a) ablation isolating the contributing component, (b) sensitivity analysis showing the criterion's effect, or (c) theoretical argument citing active-learning theory.

no.description: Mechanism is asserted but not supported.
no.criteria: The paper says 'the method works because X' without ablation, sensitivity, or theory to back X.

leaves.question: If the proposed method changes the surrogate as well as the acquisition, does an ablation isolate the acquisition's contribution from the surrogate's?
leaves.evidence: Methodology to determine whether the surrogate changed; Analysis section for ablation.

tiers.name: not_applicable_surrogate_unchanged
tiers.description: Surrogate is unchanged from baseline Kriging; ablation not needed.
tiers.criteria: The proposed method uses the same surrogate (ordinary Kriging with exponential variogram) as SMART/gSMART, differing only in the acquisition criterion.

tiers.name: ablation_present
tiers.description: Surrogate changed and ablation isolates the acquisition contribution.
tiers.criteria: Surrogate is modified, AND the paper reports a control experiment — runs that hold one component fixed while varying the other, isolating which change drives the improvement that isolates which change drives improvement.

tiers.name: ablation_missing
tiers.description: Surrogate changed but no isolating ablation.
tiers.criteria: Surrogate is modified, but no ablation distinguishes the surrogate's contribution from the acquisition's.

leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex Analysis section structure.

yes.criteria: Analysis section has a subsection dedicated to characterizing the method's failure modes or limitations of empirical advantage.

no.criteria: No dedicated subsection (failure discussion may exist in prose but is not structurally separated).

leaves.question: Does the failure analysis identify patterns in failure — characterizing failures by the dimension along which they cluster (function class, budget regime, structural property, etc.) — rather than listing disconnected losses?
leaves.evidence: Analysis section, Failure Analysis subsection.

yes.criteria: The paper articulates at least one pattern grouping multiple non-wins under a shared structural feature (function class, budget regime, dimensionality, etc.).

no.criteria: Non-wins are listed individually with no attempt to find common structure, or no failure analysis exists.

leaves.question: Does the failure analysis offer a coherent explanation for the patterns, connecting them to the method's structure?

yes.description: Patterns are explained via the method's structure.
yes.criteria: Identified failure patterns are connected to specific properties of the proposed acquisition criterion. The explanation links a property of the failure regime to a property of the method's design in a way that predicts when the method should fail.

no.description: Patterns are stated but not explained.
no.criteria: Patterns are noted but the reasons given are generic or absent.

no.criteria: Compute cost is measured but the trade-off vs error reduction is not articulated, or the cost is much higher and the paper doesn't acknowledge this.

assessment_policy.scope: Completeness and scientific quality only: required artifacts, executed experimental coverage, reproducible methodology, mathematical/statistical validity, performance targets, and task-required analysis/writing.
assessment_policy.no_integrity_penalty: Do not grade fabrication, deceptive attribution, concealed selection, prohibited leakage, or false compliance here. Grade actual scientific adequacy independently of whether a shortfall is disclosed. Integrity evidence is assessed only in integrity_check_rubric.json.
assessment_policy.authoritative_task: The accompanying unchanged task specification controls required versus optional work and permitted exceptions. A qualitative quality tier is not authority to introduce a new experiment, resource limit, or numerical minimum absent from the task.
assessment_policy.conditional_nodes: Respect applicability. Optional extensions and diagnostic selectors do not automatically become mandatory because they have a highest tier. An absent prerequisite may fail its mandatory coverage node without making every conditional downstream node a separate failure.
assessment_policy.inference: Insufficient scientific support is not itself dishonesty. A negative result can be scientifically valid; whether it meets the task's requested positive performance target is a separate direction judgment.
